scope: Additional primary-source-verified game and software projects from social search, application reimplementation, mobile ports, and platform compatibility research. See round3-review.md for provenance and boundaries.

projects.title: Cobalt (WhatsApp linked-client reimplementation)
projects.game: WhatsApp Web, Desktop, and Mobile linked-client behavior
projects.platform: Java 25/JVM applications; README lists native libraries for Windows, Linux, and macOS on x86-64 and ARM64
projects.status: The README describes the Linked client as a clean-room implementation of WhatsApp Web, Desktop, and Mobile client behavior, with separate Web-companion and Mobile-account modes. It is pre-1.0 and the maintainer expects breaking changes. The README warns that its reverse-engineered private protocol is unsupported by WhatsApp, may violate its terms, cause account restrictions, or stop working. GitHub repository metadata checked 2026-10-16 reports the last push on 2026-07-15.
projects.summary: A public Java library that lets JVM applications act as WhatsApp clients through a reverse-engineered Linked-device protocol, with Web, Desktop, and Mobile client flavors. It separately supports Meta's official WhatsApp Cloud API; the project is a protocol/client library, not a standalone messenger user interface.
projects.strategy: Clean-room implementation of WhatsApp linked-client protocols and behavior
projects.source_available: Public MIT-licensed source. The maintainer states the Linked transport uses WhatsApp's private protocol and is unofficial and unsupported; account and service availability caveats are documented in the README.
projects.subtype: Messaging client protocol and application reimplementation

projects.title: zproot (PRoot clean-room reimplementation for Android)
projects.game: PRoot user-space root emulation and Linux guest distributions on Android
projects.platform: Android devices (targetSdk 35; native aarch64 tracer), with a Zig core and Kotlin Android application
projects.status: Work in progress. The Android README says the APK builds, installs, and runs the tracer on a real device; Alpine download/extraction and end-to-end path rewriting are verified, and a static BusyBox shell works. Dynamically linked binaries are in progress; the terminal UI and multi-distribution registry have not started. The README says not to expect a usable Linux container yet. No GitHub release is listed for either repository as of 2026-10-16.
projects.summary: An Android application paired with a Zig clean-room reimplementation of PRoot. The tracer uses ptrace to intercept Linux syscalls and rewrite guest filesystem paths into an unprivileged virtual root. The Android front end has early device-tested behavior, but the project does not yet provide a usable Linux container.
projects.strategy: Clean-room Zig reimplementation of PRoot's ptrace tracer and path-translation behavior, with a Kotlin Android front end
projects.source_available: Public MIT-licensed source in separate core and Android repositories. The maintainer states no PRoot, termux-proot, or proot-distro source was read, copied, or translated. No Android app release is listed; the APK is built through the repository's CI workflow.

projects.title: SolidCraft (Fusion-style parametric CAD application)
projects.platform: Windows, macOS, Linux, and browser via WebAssembly
projects.status: The README describes SolidCraft as early but usable for simple parts. It offers desktop installers and a browser build. The maintainer reports that 75 of 76 public reference parts match selected analytic or FreeCAD-computed volume, area, centre-of-mass, and bounding-box measures; the README explicitly says those checks do not establish full geometric or workflow equivalence.
projects.summary: An independent Rust parametric CAD application with constrained sketches, a feature timeline, assemblies, sheet-metal tools, and desktop/web interfaces. The maintainers say behavior is designed from public documentation, general CAD conventions, and user feedback under clean-room contribution rules. It uses the third-party truck B-rep kernel and does not claim full Autodesk Fusion 360 compatibility or recovered Autodesk source.
projects.strategy: Clean-room implementation of Fusion-style parametric CAD workflows, with a Rust modeling engine and a third-party B-rep kernel
projects.source_available: Public source under MIT OR Apache-2.0 at the project's option. Third-party code and assets retain their own licenses; the repository documents the truck kernel and its attribution. The project states it is independent and unaffiliated with Autodesk.
projects.subtype: Desktop and web parametric 3D CAD application

projects.title: Madeira Windows PC Game Compatibility Runtime for iPhone
projects.platform: Windows x86/x86-64 games → iPhone (iOS 26+; iOS 27 supports built-in device pairing)
projects.status: Active research project; latest release v0.1.3 was published 2026-10-03. The README says many games start and some play well, while compatibility and performance vary by game. Requires an iPhone on iOS 26 or later, JIT enabled, and sideloading with an Apple ID; the built-in pairing flow requires iOS 27. This is not an App Store app because its JIT setup requires a debugger. The README does not claim a broad compatibility guarantee.
projects.summary: A single iOS app that runs unmodified Windows PC games through FEX-Emu x86/x86-64-to-ARM64 translation, Wine 11.4 built for ARM64EC (including WoW64 for 32-bit games), Direct3D 9/10/11 rendering through DXMT on Metal, and Madeira's own Direct3D 12-on-Metal implementation. Users provide their Windows game files or Steam library. Microsoft Visual C++ runtime DLLs are not bundled.
projects.strategy: Runtime CPU instruction translation (FEX-Emu) plus Wine ARM64EC/Win32 compatibility, Direct3D 9–11-to-Metal translation through DXMT, and a native Direct3D 12-on-Metal implementation.
projects.source_available: Public source under GPL-3.0-or-later with the Madeira Converter Exception. Submodule forks have component-specific licenses. The build guide requires external toolchains and setup inputs; this review did not independently reproduce a clean-checkout build. Microsoft's Visual C++ runtime DLLs are not distributed.
projects.subtype: Windows game compatibility runtime for jailed iOS

A free Apple ID signing expires after seven days. Some 64-bit games require Microsoft Visual C++ runtime DLLs that are not included.

Release notes say Cuphead, Nine Sols, and Hades II now run; these are maintainer reports, not universal compatibility guarantees.

projects.title: BattleTanx N64 Complete Matching Decompilation (TheGh0stShip)
projects.platform: Nintendo 64 (USA Rev 0, serial NBXE; 8 MiB big-endian .z64 ROM)
projects.status: The maintainer reports a complete matching decompilation, verified on 2026-10-16: 1,738/1,738 functions, 703,452/703,452 reportable code bytes, 153,924/153,924 initialized-data bytes, and all 7,335,936 bytes of the asset region accounted for. The verification document says all 1,563 matching source units passed the ROM-backed verifier. Some asset bundle entries remain semantically unidentified even though their ranges and enclosing formats are accounted for.
projects.summary: A public C and authentic source-assembly reconstruction of BattleTanx N64 USA Rev 0. The project compiles matching source units with pinned compatible toolchains and verifies them byte-for-byte against the user's own legally obtained ROM. No ROM or ROM-derived assets are included. Complete asset-region accounting does not mean every bundle entry has been semantically identified; this repository is a matching decompilation, not a PC port or static recompilation.
projects.strategy: Matching N64 decompilation using reconstructed C and authentic source assembly, compiled with pinned compatible toolchains and compared against the verified USA Rev 0 ROM; initialized data and assets are tracked in separate audited ledgers.
projects.source_available: Public GPL-3.0 project-authored source and verification/build scripts. The user must supply the supported USA Rev 0 ROM; the repository includes no ROM or ROM-derived assets. BattleTanx and its game data remain the rights holders' property.

projects.title: Gravity Rush 2 Native PC Port
projects.platform: PlayStation 4 (CUSA03694, update 01.11) → Linux x86-64 and Windows 10/11 x86-64
projects.status: Latest release checked: v2026.10.15-3159679 (2026-10-15). The README reports the opening, title, menu, and gameplay working at 30 FPS and native 1080p, with Linux tested on Nobara/Fedora 44. Windows builds are available but not yet tested in-game; saves and open-world progression remain under testing; Apple Silicon is planned.
projects.summary: Native PC port of the PS4 version of Gravity Rush 2. It runs the original x86-64 game code directly, reimplements PS4 system services, and translates Gnm graphics commands and GCN shaders to Vulkan. The user must provide the game dump and optional PS4 firmware audio library; neither is distributed.
projects.strategy: Run the original PS4 x86-64 code natively, reimplement required PS4 libraries and services, and translate Gnm commands and GCN shaders to Vulkan.
projects.source_available: Public GPL-2.0 source repository. The user must supply a legally obtained CUSA03694 game dump and, for audio, a PS4 firmware library; the project distributes neither.

projects.title: PS Switch Kit
projects.platform: PlayStation 1 matching-decompilation C → Nintendo Switch homebrew (.nro, AArch64/libnx); tested in Eden
projects.status: No release listed. The README claims that Silent Hill 1's decompiled C builds to AArch64 and reaches its warning screen in the Eden emulator using a software PSX rasterizer. The roadmap describes layer-0 build/presentation as proven and lists GTE coverage, the full game engine, main loop, title/menu/gameplay, audio/input, and validation on a second game as unfinished.
projects.summary: Reusable framework for bringing matching PlayStation decompilations to native Switch homebrew. It compiles game C for AArch64 and links it with a Psy-Q SDK shim, PSX VRAM/rasterizer runtime, and libnx platform layer. The repository is intentionally separate from any one game's decompilation.
projects.strategy: Compile matching-decompilation C for AArch64 and link it against a reusable Psy-Q shim, PSX VRAM/software-rasterizer runtime, and libnx Switch backend.
projects.source_available: Public source repository. GitHub identifies an AGPL-3.0 LICENSE file, while the README and roadmap say the kit's license is still TBD and discuss future vendored code; verify license coverage before redistribution.

projects.title: Mesa NVK Nintendo Switch Driver Port
projects.game: Mesa NVK Vulkan driver for Nintendo Switch
projects.platform: Mesa NVK / NVIDIA Tegra X1 GM20B (Maxwell) → Nintendo Switch homebrew on libnx/Horizon
projects.status: No release listed. BUILD_AND_RUN documents successful M0-M2 cross-build, Switch NRO linking, and a real-Tegra memory/submit/execute/coherency smoke test using vkCmdFillBuffer. A visible vkCmdDraw and display through the Switch window system is listed as the next milestone. projects.summary: Experimental port of Mesa's open Vulkan NVK driver to the Switch Tegra X1/GM20B. The public repository contains Mesa patches, compatibility shims, and libnx/Horizon integration intended to let Vulkan applications use the Switch GPU without a proprietary NVIDIA blob.
projects.strategy: Port Mesa NVK to Switch Tegra hardware with Mesa patches and Switch-specific memory, submission, compatibility, and window-system integration over libnx/Horizon.
projects.source_available: Public GPL-2.0-or-later repository with Mesa/NVK-derived portions under their original MIT/Apache-2.0 terms. Build scripts, patches, shims, and status documents are public; no release binaries were listed.

projects.title: ARMSX2 Nintendo Switch Port
projects.status: Latest release checked: v3.0.0 (2026-08-24). The README warns that general playable performance is not expected and names the PS2 BIOS, load screens, and MegaMan Legacy Collection as the only observed full-speed examples. The release reports about a 50% improvement across a small tested set and adds OpenGL, USB loading, multiplayer, Vulkan shader cache, and AArch64 MMI recompilers.

projects.strategy: Adapt the ARMSX2 PlayStation 2 emulator for Switch hardware and package a native homebrew .nro with Switch-specific graphics and input support.
